card.title: Heisenberg's Uncertainty Principle and concept of probability

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Heisenberg's uncertainty principle: Δx·Δp_x ≥ h/4π = ħ/2 (position-momentum); ΔE·Δt ≥ ħ/2 (energy-time); ΔL_x·ΔL_y ≥ ħ|⟨L_z⟩|/2 (angular momentum). Fundamental from [x,p]=iħ, not instrumental. Bohr orbit: exact r,v → Δx·Δp=0 forbidden; n=1 gives Δp/p≈50%. Energy-time: ΔE·Δt≥ħ/2 → finite τ gives ΔE=ħ/τ (natural line width, Lorentzian). Electron in nucleus: Δx=1 fm → K≥9.5 MeV → impossible (atomic eV vs nuclear MeV).…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Δx·Δp_x ≥ h/4π = ħ/2 (position-momentum)
ΔE·Δt ≥ h/4π = ħ/2 (energy-time)
ΔL_x·ΔL_y ≥ ħ|⟨L_z⟩|/2 (angular momentum)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ❌ Uncertainty principle is a limitation of measuring instruments. ✅ Fundamental property from [x,p]=iħ; even perfect instruments cannot circumvent it.  ·  ❌ The constant is h/2π. ✅ It is h/4π = ħ/2; h/2π is the classic 1-mark trap.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Δx·Δp_x ≥ h/4π = ħ/2 (position-momentum uncertainty).  ·  ΔE·Δt ≥ h/4π = ħ/2 (energy-time uncertainty).

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: n=1 hydrogen: Δx ≈ a₀ = 5.29×10⁻¹¹ m → Δp ≥ 1.05×10⁻²⁴ kg·m/s → Δp/p ≈ 50%.  ·  Electron confined to 10⁻¹⁰ m: Δv ≥ 5.78×10⁵ m/s.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Covers only: Heisenberg's Uncertainty Principle, concept of probability, applications (within Atomic Structure).  ·  Out of scope: detailed commutator algebra, relativistic uncertainty, QFT — later topics.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: ΔL_x·ΔL_y ≥ ħ|⟨L_z⟩|/2 (angular momentum uncertainty).  ·  Bohr orbit impossible: exact r,v → Δx·Δp=0 forbidden; n=1 gives Δp/p ≈ 50%.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: SHORT (2 marks): State and explain Heisenberg's uncertainty principle; why is it not a limit of instruments?  ·  SHORT (3 marks): Show that a definite Bohr orbit is inconsistent with the uncertainty principle.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: ❌ ΔE·Δt ≥ ħ/2 comes from [E,t] = iħ commutator. ✅ Time is a parameter, not an operator in non-relativistic QM; the relation comes from Fourier transform.  ·  ❌ Electron can exist in nucleus if energy is high enough. ✅ Atomic energies ~ eV; nuclear binding ~ MeV; electron would need ~10 MeV — impossible in atom.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Δx·Δp_x ≥ h/4π = ħ/2 (position-momentum); fundamental from [x,p]=iħ, not instrumental.  ·  ΔE·Δt ≥ ħ/2 (energy-time); finite lifetime τ gives ΔE = ħ/τ → natural line width (Lorentzian).  ·  Electron in nucleus: Δx=1 fm → Δp≥5.27×10⁻²⁰ kg·m/s → K≥9.5 MeV → impossible (atomic eV vs nuclear MeV).  ·  Probability: ψ = amplitude; |ψ|² = probability density (Born rule); replaces definite trajectory.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Energy-time: ΔE = ħ/τ for finite lifetime τ → natural line width (Lorentzian).

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: SHORT (3 marks): Explain the concept of probability and the meaning of |ψ|² in the quantum-mechanical atom.  ·  SHORT (3 marks): An electron is confined to 10⁻¹⁰ m; estimate the minimum uncertainty in its velocity.  ·  SHORT (3 marks): Use ΔE·Δt ≥ h/4π to explain line broadening for an excited-state lifetime of 10⁻⁸ s.

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: Excited state τ = 10⁻⁸ s → ΔE = 6.6×10⁻⁸ eV; Δν = 1.6×10⁷ Hz; Lorentzian line shape.  ·  Nucleus radius 1 fm: electron would need ~10 MeV → impossible (atomic eV vs nuclear MeV).

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: The uncertainty principle is significant for: → B  ·  The uncertainty principle is a consequence of: → B

rows.text: # Heisenberg's Uncertainty Principle and concept of probability ## 1. Topic Introduction Werner Heisenberg's 1927 uncertainty principle is the most famous consequence of quantum mechanics — and the most misunderstood. It is not a limitation of measuring instruments; it is a fundamental property of nature.…  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Conceptual Understanding ### What the uncertainty principle is The Heisenberg uncertainty principle states that certain pairs of complementary observables cannot be simultaneously determined with arbitrary precision.…  ·  ## 3. rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Δθ·ΔL_z ≥ ħ/2 (angle-angular momentum)  ·  [x, p_x] = iħ (commutator → uncertainty)  ·  Δp ≥ ħ/2Δx (from uncertainty principle)

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Δv = Δp/m = ħ/(2mΔx) (velocity uncertainty)  ·  ΔE ≥ ħ/2Δt (energy-time uncertainty)  ·  ΔE = ħ/τ (natural line width, τ = lifetime)

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Δν = 1/2πτ (natural line width in frequency)  ·  Δλ = λ²/(2πcτ) (natural line width in wavelength)  ·  K = (Δp)²/2m (kinetic energy from momentum uncertainty)

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: κ = √(2m(V-E))/ħ (tunneling decay constant)  ·  T ≈ exp(-2κL) (tunneling transmission probability)  ·  E₀ = ½ħω (zero-point energy for harmonic oscillator)

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ΔE·Δt ≥ ħ/2 → virtual particles ΔE for time Δt ≤ ħ/2ΔE  ·  Zero-point energy E₀ = ½ħω; molecules vibrate even at 0 K.  ·  Tunneling: ψ ~ exp(-κx) in barrier; κ = √(2m(V-E))/ħ; T ~ exp(-2κL).
